gloss: false accusation case; wrongful conviction case

definitions.gloss: false accusation case; wrongful conviction case; miscarriage of justice
definitions.explanation: A criminal case in which an innocent person is wrongfully accused, convicted, or punished for a crime they did not commit.

examples.japanese: {冤罪事件|えんざいじけん}が{発覚|はっかく}した。
examples.english: A wrongful conviction case came to light.

examples.japanese: DNA{鑑定|かんてい}によって{冤罪事件|えんざいじけん}が{証明|しょうめい}され、{被告人|ひこくにん}は{釈放|しゃくほう}された。
examples.english: Through DNA testing, the wrongful conviction was proven and the defendant was released.

examples.japanese: {何十年|なんじゅうねん}もの{投獄|とうごく}を{経|へ}て{冤罪事件|えんざいじけん}の{再審|さいしん}が{認|みと}められ、{社会|しゃかい}に{大|おお}きな{衝撃|しょうげき}を{与|あた}えた。
examples.english: After decades of imprisonment, a retrial for the wrongful conviction case was granted, sending shockwaves through society.

notes:
A compound of {冤罪|えんざい} (false charge, wrongful conviction) and {事件|じけん} (incident, case). Japan has had several high-profile {冤罪事件|えんざいじけん}, some involving decades of imprisonment before exoneration.

The topic is significant in Japanese legal discourse because Japan's criminal justice system has a conviction rate of over 99%, leading to debates about whether wrongful convictions are adequately prevented.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冤罪事件|えんざいじけん}の{再審|さいしん}: retrial of a wrongful conviction case
- {冤罪事件|えんざいじけん}を{防|ふせ}ぐ: to prevent wrongful convictions
- {冤罪事件|えんざいじけん}の{被害者|ひがいしゃ}: victim of a wrongful conviction
- {冤罪事件|えんざいじけん}が{相次|あいつ}ぐ: wrongful conviction cases occur one after another

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {冤罪|えんざい}: false charge, wrongful conviction — the condition itself, without specifying it as a case
- {誤認|ごにん}{逮捕|たいほ}: mistaken arrest — being arrested for the wrong person or crime
- {無実|むじつ}: innocence — the state of being not guilty
